messages:
sam: Quick sync: we discovered a ton of legacy saved queries without scope metadata. UX expected behavior is unclear. Thoughts on migration?

elaine: Oof. So legacy saves are just filters blob + name, no scope. If we naively default to org scope we risk breaking per-route dashboards.

diego: Proposal: run a migration pass to infer scope from the saved filters. If the filter contains `route` or `route_id` -> mark route scoped; if it has `model` or `model_tag` and no route -> model scoped; otherwise org.

hao: Be careful: some saved queries reference deprecated route names that were renamed in the last routing refactor. We'll need a fuzzy match table or alias map.

sam: Right. We already have a route_aliases table in infra. Diego can we use that in migration?

diego: Yep, migration will consult route_aliases and model_tag registry. If ambiguous, flag for manual review and default to org but mark `migration_inferred=false`.

tara: UX: For migrated items we should show a small "inferred scope" badge with a tooltip: "Inferred during migration; click to confirm". Users can then explicitly change scope.

elaine: Also add an audit column `migrated_at` and `migrated_by` so we can trace back.

h ao: backend: we must ensure the migration is idempotent and rate limited. Some customers have 100k saved queries. Do it in batches and emit progress metrics.

infra-bot: Started job MIGRATE-QUERY-SCOPE-2026. Estimated runtime 3h.

sam: Dashboard behavior: if a dashboard references a saved query that becomes model-scoped, what should happen? I think dashboards should prefer explicitness: if dashboard was created in a route context, keep applying route-level filter. If not, leave it as-is but surface mismatch.

diego: Implementation detail: saved_query record will gain fields `scope`, `route_id`, `model_tag`, `migration_status`. We'll add a lightweight `scope_hint` for the client to display without extra lookups.

elaine: Telemetry we need: migration_outcome (inferred/ambiguous/manual), original_filter_signature, user_confirmed_scope later. Also log dashboard_apply_mismatch when dashboard context != saved_query.scope.

hao: ACLs: if a saved query is migrated to route scope and references route-only data, ensure only users with route access see it. We'll re-evaluate visibility during migration and mark inaccessible items as `private`.

tara: UX microflow: on first open of a migrated saved query show a non-blocking banner: "We inferred this as route-scoped for /payments. Confirm? [Keep inferred] [Edit scope] [Always treat as org]". Keep it dismissible.

sam: What about quick-save behavior moving forward? We discussed quick-save shortcuts last week. I propose a default heuristic: on route page -> default route; on model page -> default model; on global list -> org. Quick-save uses that default.

diego: Make sure quick-save sets `origin: quick` and `ui_hint: keyboard` in telemetry.

elaine: Also a small UI change: saved query list should show scope icons and a muted subtitle if scope != current page. That reduces accidental applies.

hao: API change: add PATCH /saved-queries/:id/scope to allow changing scope without re-saving filters. Must validate route_id exists and user has access.

tara: For rollout plan: start migration in staging, enable inferred badges, collect metrics for 2 weeks, then ramp to prod with a rollback plan.

infra-bot: Job MIGRATE-QUERY-SCOPE-2026: batch 1 completed (2.4k items). Errors: 12 ambiguous -> flagged.

sam: Nice. Diego, please open the migration PR + runbook. Elaine, we'll coordinate the banner copy. Tara, add rollout steps to the roadmap.
